title.en: Did Trump really rescue Venezuela? – podcast
title.zh: 特朗普真的“拯救”了委内瑞拉吗？——播客

summary.en: The Guardian's Latin America correspondent, Tom Phillips, discusses the situation in Venezuela four months after the US abduction of former president Nicolás Maduro and a disputed presidential election, exploring the impact on daily life.
summary.zh: 《卫报》拉丁美洲记者汤姆·菲利普斯探讨了美国“绑架”前总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗和一场有争议的总统选举四个月后，委内瑞拉的局势，并审视了这对当地日常生活的影响。

body.en: Tom Phillips on life in the country four months after the US abduction of the former president Nicolás Maduro “The last time I flew out of Venezuela was right at the start of August 2024, just after the disputed presidential election,” the Guardian’s Latin America correspondent, Tom Phillips , tells Annie Kelly . “It was a moment of real turmoil. There was a huge wave of repression that was unfolding as Nicolás Maduro tried to silence any kind of dissent to his bogus claim to have won that election. Thousands were thrown in prison, many were going underground, and journalists were racing to get out of the country.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 汤姆·菲利普斯 (Tom Phillips) 讲述美国绑架前总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗 (Nicolás Maduro) 四个月后在委内瑞拉的生活“我上次飞出委内瑞拉是在 2024 年 8 月初，就在有争议的总统选举之后，”《卫报》拉丁美洲记者汤姆·菲利普斯 (Tom Phillips) 告诉安妮·凯利 (Annie Kelly)。 “那是一个真正的动荡时刻。当尼古拉斯·马杜罗试图压制任何对其虚假声称赢得选举的异议时，一股巨大的镇压浪潮正在展开。数千人被投入监狱，许多人转入地下，记者们竞相逃离这个国家。”继续阅读...

reflection.en: The question of whether a nation has been 'rescued' often comes down to the lived experience of its people under new leadership. Proverbs reminds us that the true measure of governance is reflected in the joy or sorrow of the populace. As we consider the state of Venezuela, this verse invites us to look beyond political narratives to the actual well-being...
reflection.zh: 一个国家是否被“拯救”，往往取决于其人民在新领导下的生活体验。箴言提醒我们，衡量治理的真正标准反映在民众的喜乐或悲叹之中。当我们思考委内瑞拉的现状时，这节经文邀请我们超越政治叙事，关注其公民的实际福祉。

verse.textEn: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.
verse.textZh: 义人增多，民就喜乐；恶人掌权，民就叹息。

title.en: ‘They decided to buy the seat’: Massie speaks out after losing House primary to Trump-backed challenger Ed Gallrein – live
title.zh: 特朗普在德克萨斯州支持帕克斯顿，再次抨击肯塔基州的马西，六个州举行初选——美国政治直播

summary.en: Former President Trump endorsed Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in the state's Senate primary, backing a hardline ally over a veteran senator. This contest, along with primaries in five other states, is seen as a test of the former president's influence within the Republican Party.
summary.zh: 前总统特朗普在德克萨斯州参议院初选中支持州总检察长肯·帕克斯顿，选择了一位强硬派盟友而非资深参议员。这场竞争，连同其他五个州的初选，被视为对前总统在共和党内影响力的最新考验。

body.en: Kentucky congressman who championed Epstein bill failed to fight off attacks from president in victory for Trump Trump critic Thomas Massie defeated in Kentucky Republican House primary Sign up for the Breaking News US email Trump told reporters he is giving Iran until the weekend or early next week , to make a deal to end the war. He said that yesterday he was within an hour of deciding to resume bombing Iran but that his negotiators had reported progress in talks. I never tell anybody when. But they knew that we were very close. I would say we were. I was an hour away from making the decision to go today, and we would probably not be talking about a beautiful ballroom today. We’d be talking about that. I had made the decision, so they called up. They had heard I made the decision. They said, sir, could you give us a couple of more days because we think they’re being reasonable. Well, I mean, I’m saying 2 or 3 days, maybe Friday, Saturday, Sunday something. Maybe early next week, a limited period of time, because we can’t let them have a new nuclear weapon. Continue reading...
body.zh: 特朗普在得克萨斯州参议院初选中支持总检察长肯·帕克斯顿（Ken Paxton），特朗普告诉记者，他将在周末或下周初之前与伊朗达成协议以结束战争。他表示，昨天他距离决定恢复轰炸伊朗不到一个小时，但他的谈判代表已经报告了谈判取得的进展。我从来不告诉任何人什么时候。但他们知道我们非常接近。我想说我们是。距离我今天做出去的决定还有一个小时，我们今天可能不会谈论一个美丽的舞厅。我们会谈论这个。我已经做出了决定，所以他们给我打电话了。他们听说我做了这个决定。他们说，先生，您能否再给我们几天时间，因为我们认为他们是合理的。嗯，我的意思是，我说的是两三天，也许周五、周六、周日什么的。也许下周初，一段有限的时间，因为我们不能让他们拥有新的核武器。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Political endorsements and primary elections highlight the significant choices citizens face in selecting their leaders. Proverbs 29:2 reminds us that the character of those in authority profoundly impacts the well-being of a society. As communities engage in these decisions, there is a shared hope for leaders who will serve with integrity and wisdom,...
reflection.zh: 政治背书和初选凸显了公民在选择领导人时面临的重要抉择。箴言29:2提醒我们，掌权者的品格深刻影响着社会的福祉。当社区参与这些决策时，人们共同希望选出正直和智慧的领导人，营造一个所有人都能繁荣发展的环境。

title.en: Trump critic Thomas Massie defeated in Kentucky Republican House primary
title.zh: 特朗普批评者托马斯·马西在肯塔基州共和党众议院初选中落败

summary.en: Thomas Massie, a critic of Donald Trump, was defeated in the Kentucky Republican House primary. Massie alleged that his opponents 'bought the seat,' while the victory for Ed Gallrein demonstrated the president's strong influence within the party.
summary.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普的批评者托马斯·马西在肯塔基州共和党众议院初选中落败。马西声称对手“买下了席位”，而埃德·加尔雷因的胜利则显示了总统在该党内的强大影响力。

body.en: Massie says opponents ‘decided to buy the seat’ as victory for Ed Gallrein shows strength of president’s grip on party Midterm primaries – live updates Donald Trump displayed his supremacy over the Republican party on Tuesday when voters in northern Kentucky rejected the maverick congressman Thomas Massie in favour of the US president’s hand-picked challenger. Ed Gallrein, a retired navy Seal and farmer who was recruited into the race by Trump, defeated the seven-term incumbent in a primary election in Kentucky’s fourth congressional district in what the president’s allies framed as a test of whether dissent could still exist inside today’s Republican party. Continue reading...
body.zh: 马西表示，对手“决定买下这个席位”，因为艾德·加莱因的胜利显示了总统对党内中期初选的控制力。周二，肯塔基州北部的选民拒绝了特立独行的国会议员托马斯·马西，转而支持美国总统精心挑选的挑战者，唐纳德·特朗普展示了他对共和党的至高无上的地位。埃德·加莱因 (Ed Gallrein) 是一名退役海军海豹突击队员和农民，被特朗普招募参加竞选，他在肯塔基州第四国会选区的初选中击败了七届现任总统，总统的盟友认为这是对当今共和党内部是否仍然存在异议的考验。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Political contests often highlight the intense struggle for power and influence, with outcomes that can feel decisive and absolute. Yet, Psalm 75:7 reminds us that while human leaders rise and fall, it is God who ultimately judges, exalting one and bringing down another. This perspective encourages us to look beyond the immediate political landscape,...
reflection.zh: 政治竞争常常凸显权力与影响力的激烈争夺，其结果可能令人感到决定性和绝对。然而，诗篇75:7提醒我们，尽管人类领袖有兴有衰，最终的审判者是神，祂使人高升，也使人降卑。这一视角鼓励我们超越眼前的政治格局，信靠超越世俗权力动态的神圣主权。

verse.textEn: It is God who judges: He brings one down, he exalts another.
verse.textZh: 惟有神断定；他使这人降卑，使那人升高。

reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到公义、尊严与问责。Micah 6:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以带着怜悯的公义来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: Father-of-eight killed in San Diego mosque shooting hailed as hero
title.zh: 圣地亚哥清真寺枪击案中遇害的八个孩子的父亲被誉为英雄

summary.en: Security guard Amin Abdullah, a father of eight, was among three people killed in a mosque attack in San Diego. He was remembered by officials as "a shining light" and hailed as a hero.
summary.zh: 安全警卫阿明·阿卜杜拉是圣地亚哥清真寺袭击中遇难的三人之一，他是一位八个孩子的父亲。官员们称赞他为“一道闪亮的光”，并尊他为英雄。

body.en:
The bravery of a security guard who was shot dead along with two other worshippers at a San Diego mosque on Monday prevented the attack from being much worse, say police.

The guard was Amin Abdullah, a father of eight, a spokeswoman for the Council on American-Islamic Relations-San Diego (Cair-SD), Tazheen Nizam, told the BBC.

"It's fair to say his actions were heroic," San Diego Police Chief Scott Wahl told a news conference. "Undoubtedly, he saved lives today."

Abdullah and two others - whom Cair-SD named as Mansour Kaziha and Nader Awad - were killed by two yet-to-be-identified teenage attackers who then took their own lives, say police.

Police said on Tuesday that as the suspects ran passed Abdullah at the mosque's entrance he began shooting, and they returned fire.

He also enacted lockdown procedures and is credited with saving numerous lives, including those of 140 children at the school that is part of the centre, Wahl said at a briefing on Tuesday.

The two other victims then drew the attention of the suspects in a parking lot, where they were fatally shot. Wahl said the response that Abdullah initiated "undoubtedly" pushed the suspects to flee.

People who knew Abdullah told US media he looked after the community. Others have taken to social media to describe him as "the nicest man you'll ever meet".

The mosque called him "a courageous man who put himself on the line of the safety of others, who even in his last moments did not stop protecting our community".

Nizam, the Cair spokeswoman, told the BBC: "Amin was loved by everybody, he stood there day after day, always smiling, welcoming everybody, welcoming the kids who came to the school.

A friend of the family told the Associated Press that Abdullah was well-known at the mosque and had worked there for more than a decade.

"He wanted to defend the innocent so he decided to become a security guard," Shaykh Uthman Ibn Farooq told the news agency.

Sam Hamideh knew Abdullah through the mosque and told the BBC's US news partner CBS that the security guard would be remembered for his kindness.

"It didn't matter who walked up... any random person could just walk up and, like, [Abdullah] would greet them, make sure they are OK," Hamideh said.

"Whether they were homeless off the street looking for something, whether it was a child or elderly."

On Tuesday evening, ahead of a community vigil, his daughter Hawa Abdullah, flanked by her siblings, said her father "would want our community to stand together as one".

"That's exactly the legacy he left behind. He wants all of us to be better, regardless of who we are, what we identify as," she added.

The family was joined by several members of the San Diego Islamic community, many of whom called on elected officials to be careful in how they...
body.zh: 警方称，周一在圣地亚哥一座清真寺与另外两名礼拜者一起被枪杀的一名保安的英勇行为避免了袭击变得更加严重。 圣地亚哥美国伊斯兰关系委员会 (Cair-SD) 发言人塔兹恩·尼扎姆 (Tazheen Nizam) 告诉 BBC，这名警卫是阿明·阿卜杜拉 (Amin Abdullah)，他是八个孩子的父亲。 圣地亚哥警察局长斯科特·瓦尔在新闻发布会上说：“可以公平地说，他的行为是英勇的。” “毫无疑问，他今天拯救了生命。” 警方称，阿卜杜拉和另外两人（Cair-SD 称其为曼苏尔·卡齐哈 (Mansour Kaziha) 和纳德·阿瓦德 (Nader Awad)）被两名身份不明的青少年袭击者杀害，随后他们自杀了。 认识阿卜杜拉的人告诉美国媒体，他照顾社区。其他人在社交媒体上形容他是“你见过的最好的人”。 清真寺称他为“一个勇敢的人，他将自己置于他人的安全线上，即使在他的最后时刻也没有停止保护我们的社区”。 凯尔发言人尼扎姆告诉英国广播公司：“阿明受到每个人的喜爱，他日复一日地站在那里，总是微笑着欢迎所有人，欢迎来到学校的孩子们。 这家人的一位朋友告诉美联社，阿卜杜拉在这座清真寺很有名，并在那里工作了十多年。 “他想保护无辜者，所以他决定成为一名保安，”谢赫·奥斯曼·伊本·法鲁克告诉新闻社。 萨姆·哈米德通过清真寺认识了阿卜杜拉，并告诉英国广播公司美国新闻合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司，人们会记住这名保安的善良。 哈米德说：“谁走过来并不重要……任何随机的人都可以走过来，就像[阿卜杜拉]会向他们打招呼，确保他们没事。” “无论他们是无家可归的人在街上寻找什么东西，无论是孩子还是老人。” Cair-SD 表示，另外两名受害者是清真寺的礼拜者。卡齐哈帮助维护其场地和便利店。阿瓦德的妻子在一所伊斯兰中心的学校任教。 周一中午，这起致命枪击事件发生，两名涉嫌袭击者之一的母亲打电话给警方，报告说她的儿子与朋友私奔，可能有自杀倾向。 几小时后，当警方搜寻这两名青少年时，当局在圣地亚哥伊斯兰中心外发现了三名受枪伤的受害者，其中包括阿卜杜拉。 不久之后，警方在距离清真寺几个街区外的一辆汽车中发现了两名分别为 17 岁和 18 岁的嫌疑人，他们自伤身亡。 瓦尔说，这起枪击事件正在作为仇恨犯罪进行调查，并指出其中涉及“仇恨言论”。 美国副总统万斯周二在白宫对记者发表讲话，称枪击事件“应受谴责”，并鼓励美国人为每个人祈祷……

reflection.en: The tragic loss of Amin Abdullah, a father and a "shining light," reminds us of the profound pain and grief that senseless violence inflicts. In moments of such deep sorrow, we hold onto the promise that one day, all tears will be wiped away, and death and suffering will be no more. This hope offers solace even as we mourn the present darkness.
reflection.zh: 阿明·阿卜杜拉这位父亲和“一道闪亮的光”的悲惨逝去，提醒我们毫无意义的暴力所带来的深切痛苦和悲伤。在如此深重的悲痛时刻，我们紧紧抓住那应许，即有一天，所有的眼泪都将被擦去，死亡和苦难将不复存在。这份盼望在哀悼当下的黑暗时，仍能带来慰藉。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: Trump says Iran wants a peace deal but warns US may strike again
title.zh: 特朗普称伊朗希望达成和平协议，但警告美国可能再次发动袭击

summary.en: President Donald Trump warns the US may strike Iran again, a day after he claims he held off a major assault in hopes of a peace deal.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
President Donald Trump says the United States may need to strike Iran again, and that he has been an hour away from ordering an attack before postponing it.

Trump made the comments a day after saying he had paused a planned resumption of hostilities following a new proposal by Tehran to end the US-Israeli war.

"I was an hour away from making the decision to go today," Trump told reporters at the White House on Tuesday.

Iran's leaders are begging for a deal, he said, adding that a new US attack would happen in coming days if no agreement was reached.

The United States has been struggling to end the war it began with Israel nearly three months ago. Trump has previously said that a deal with Tehran was close, and similarly threatened heavy strikes on Iran if it did not reach an accord.

The US president is under intense political pressure at home to reach an accord that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz — a key route for global supplies of oil and other commodities. Gas prices remain high and Trump's approval rating has plummeted as congressional elections loom in November.

Oil prices settled lower on Tuesday after Vice President JD Vance said Washington and Tehran had made a lot of progress in talks and neither side wanted to see a resumption of the military campaign. "We're in a pretty good spot here," he said.

Speaking to reporters at a White House briefing, Vance acknowledged difficulties in negotiating with a fractured Iranian leadership. "It's not sometimes totally clear what the negotiating position of the team is," he said, so the US is trying to make its own red lines clear.

He also said one objective of Trump's policy is to prevent a nuclear arms race from spreading in the region.

In Tehran, Ebrahim Azizi, head of the Iranian parliament's national security committee, said on X that pausing an attack was due to Trump's realisation that any move against Iran would mean "facing a decisive military response".

Iranian state media said Tehran's latest peace proposal involves ending hostilities on all fronts including Lebanon, the exit of US forces from areas close to Iran, and reparations for destruction caused by the US-Israeli attacks.

Tehran also sought the lifting of sanctions, release of frozen funds and an end to the US marine blockade, according to Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi as cited by IRNA news agency.

The terms as described in the Iranian reports appeared little changed from Iran's previous offer, which Trump rejected last week as "garbage".

Reuters could not determine whether military preparations had been made for strikes that would mark a renewal of the war Trump started in late February.

title.en: WHO 'deeply concerned about scale and speed' of deadly Ebola outbreak
title.zh: 世卫组织对致命埃博拉疫情的规模和速度深感担忧

summary.en: The World Health Organization says 26 more suspected Ebola deaths have been recorded in 24 hours.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The World Health Organization says it's worried about the "scale and speed" of an Ebola outbreak that has killed more than 130 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo and warns it could be lengthy.

Ebola has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa in the past half-century and the UN health agency has declared the latest surge of the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever an international health emergency.

No vaccine or therapeutic treatment exists for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola that is responsible for the outbreak — the 17th in the vast central African country of more than 100 million people.

Workers with shovels were seen digging to clear an abandoned Ebola treatment centre in the eastern city of Goma.

"We are currently spreading sand and preparing the site to help care for people affected by Ebola virus disease," said Philippe Jamaica, who was supervising the work.

Tonnes of emergency medical supplies, including infection prevention kits and tents, as well as experts have arrived in recent days, local WHO footage showed.

With the recent cases largely concentrated in difficult-to-access areas hit by long-running conflicts, few samples have been laboratory-tested and figures are based mostly on suspected cases.

Congolese Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba told reporters on Tuesday that there had been 136 deaths suspected to be linked to Ebola and about 543 suspected cases, calling for international aid to help combat the spread.

WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said he was "deeply concerned about the scale and speed of the epidemic" while the agency's representative in the DRC said a vaccine candidate called Ervebo was being considered.

But Anne Ancia said it would likely take at least two months to be available, adding: "I don't think that in two months we will be done with this outbreak".

At the hospital in Rwampara in northeastern Ituri province, the epicentre of the outbreak near the border with Uganda and South Sudan, the response was slow, despite the surge in cases.

"We dig graves and bury people who died without gloves or any protection. We're so exposed," Salama Bamunoba, from a local youth organisation, told AFP.

"We're already at about 100 cases. We didn't have an appropriate place to do triage and isolate suspected cases" until Monday, said one local hospital official.

Kamba told reporters that equipment was being delivered. "We have everything healthcare providers will need," he added.

The DRC's deadliest Ebola outbreak, between 2018 and 2020, claimed nearly 2,300 lives from 3,500 cases.

The east is a gold-mining hub with people regularly crisscrossing the region, and it has been plagued by clashes between local militias for years.

title.en: Singer Patrick Bruel denies wave of sexual assault allegations in France
title.zh: 歌手帕特里克·布鲁尔否认在法国的性侵指控浪潮

summary.en: Singer Patrick Bruel is denying multiple allegations of sexual assault in France. Among the accusers is TV and radio presenter Flavie Flament, who claims he raped her in 1991.
summary.zh: 歌手帕特里克·布鲁尔否认了在法国对他提出的一系列性侵指控。其中一位指控者是知名电视电台主持人弗拉维·弗拉芒，她声称布鲁尔在1991年强奸了她。

body.en:
French star Patrick Bruel has fiercely denied allegations he sexually assaulted a number of women during his 50-year career as a singer and actor.

Bruel, 67, has in recent weeks been the subject of a wave of accusations – some of which are now being examined by prosecutors with a view to possible court action.

Among his latest accusers is the well-known TV and radio presenter Flavie Flament, who alleges the singer drugged and raped her at his Paris home in 1991, when she was 16 and he 32.

Bruel, who is currently performing at a Paris theatre, wrote in a post on Instagram that he had never in his life "forced myself on a woman".

"Nor have I ever drugged, manipulated or tried to subjugate anyone… nor used my fame to abuse or obtain non-consensual relations," he said.

Born Patrick Benguigui in Algeria in 1959, Bruel came to fame in the early 1980s with songs such as Marre de cette nana-là (Had enough of that chick). His strong voice and dark brooding looks led to a public obsession that became known as Bruelmania.

He has remained in the public eye and the abuse allegations against him have been making front-page news in France.

Bruel is due to start a concert tour in June of France, Belgium, Switzerland and Canada after finishing his theatre engagement, but a feminist group has launched an online petition to have the tour cancelled.

In addition to Flament, around 30 other women have complained about sexual mistreatment by Bruel, according to French investigative website Mediapart.

Around 10 of these cases are now being reviewed by prosecutors in the Paris suburb of Nanterre. They include a case that was initially dropped in 2020 for lack of evidence. Two separate allegations are being studied in the Brittany town of Saint-Mâlo and in Belgium.

French government spokeswoman Maud Bregeon said on Tuesday that female victims should be encouraged to speak out "even decades later", adding "it is up then up to the justice system to establish the truth of the facts".

Flament told Mediapart that Bruel "set his heart" on her after they met on the set of a TV programme, and one day invited her back to his flat.

She said she remembered drinking a cup of tea, and the next thing Bruel was "doing up my trousers as I lay on his bed". Flament said she was convinced she had been drugged and raped.

On Tuesday, Bruel's lawyer Christophe Ingrain said the story was made up and the relationship between his client and Flament had been "totally consensual".

"Patrick Bruel is very clear: he never forced himself on or drugged Flavie Flament. There was no rape," Ingrain told BFMTV.

"They were two people who liked each other and might from time to time have sex when they met," he added.

title.en: Ebola outbreak may be spreading faster than first thought, WHO doctor warns
title.zh: 世卫组织医生警告：埃博拉病毒传播速度可能超出预期

summary.en: A World Health Organization doctor has warned that Ebola may be spreading more rapidly than initially estimated in central Africa, with experts concerned that the actual number of cases could be significantly higher than the hundreds currently suspected.
summary.zh: 世界卫生组织的一位医生警告说，埃博拉病毒在中非地区的传播速度可能比最初估计的要快，专家们担心实际病例数可能远高于目前数百例的疑似病例。

body.en:
People living close to the epicentre of a deadly Ebola outbreak have told the BBC of their fear, as the World Health Organization (WHO) warned cases may be spreading faster than originally thought.

One man in the Democratic Republic of Congo's northeastern Ituri province said infected people were dying "very fast", adding: "Ebola has tortured us."

The virus is believed to have killed 136 people in the DR Congo, officials say, with more than 514 cases now suspected in the country. One person has died in neighbouring Uganda.

The WHO's Dr Anne Ancia told the BBC that the more the UN agency investigates the outbreak, the clearer it becomes cases have spread to other areas.

Modelling by the London-based MRC Centre for Global Infectious Disease Analysis released on Monday suggested there had been "substantial" under-detection, and that it could not rule out there had already been more than 1,000 cases.

The study suggested that the current outbreak is "larger than currently ascertained" and that its "true magnitude remains uncertain".

A man who spoke to BBC News and identified himself as Bigboy said people are "really scared" and doing what they can to protect themselves.

He said locals are taking precautions such as washing hands with clean water, but added that he wished they could get access to other protective supplies such as face masks.

Another Ituri local, Alfred Giza, said people in the community are aware of the threat and waiting to receive face masks to protect themselves, but that he would not know what to do if a family member or friend contracted the disease.

The Red Cross warned that Ebola can escalate quickly if cases are not identified early, communities lack information and health systems are overwhelmed, adding "we are seeing all those conditions" in the current outbreak.

On Tuesday, DR Congo President Félix Tshisekedi called for "calm" and urged Congolese citizens to remain vigilant, after holding a crisis meeting on Monday evening.

WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, who declared the outbreak an international emergency last week, said he was "deeply concerned about the scale and speed of the epidemic".

He declared the emergency late on Saturday night - before the WHO's emergency committee met to assess the situation and recommend priority medical interventions, which it is due to do soon.

The cash-strapped organisation has already released almost $4m (£3m) to combat the outbreak - but much more may be needed.

The outbreak is taking place in a region which has suffered years of conflict, with hospitals and clinics damaged or destroyed, and millions fleeing their homes. Most are living in unsanitary conditions.

title.en: Estonia says Nato jet shot down drone over its territory
title.zh: 爱沙尼亚称北约飞机在其领空击落一架无人机

summary.en: Estonia reported that a NATO jet shot down a drone over its territory, which officials suspect was a Ukrainian projectile diverted by Russian electronic jamming.
summary.zh: 爱沙尼亚报告称，一架北约飞机在其领空击落了一架无人机，官员怀疑这架无人机是受俄罗斯电子干扰而偏离航线的乌克兰射弹。

body.en:
Estonia has said a Nato fighter jet shot down a drone, which it suspects was a Ukrainian projectile knocked off course by Russian electronic jamming, over its territory.

Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur said a Romanian F-16 fired a missile and drone debris fell in a marshy area in central Estonia on Tuesday. No damage was reported.

Ukraine reacted by accusing Russia of deliberately redirecting Ukrainian drones launched at "legitimate military targets" in Russia, apologising to "Estonia and all of our Baltic friends for such unintended incidents".

Russia has not commented on the latest in a series of recent drone incursions over Nato members Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.

Last week, Latvian Prime Minister Evika Silina resigned following a political crisis over Russia-bound Ukrainian drones straying into Latvian territory.

Earlier this month, two Ukrainian drones hit an empty oil storage site in Latvia. Ukraine said this was the result of electronic jamming by Russia.

Moscow has accused the three Baltic states of allowing Ukraine to use their "air corridors" to strike targets inside Russia - a claimed denied by Tallinn, Riga and Vilnius.

Ukraine has recently intensified its drone and missile attacks against targets in Russia, including oil and gas facilities near the Baltic states.

Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

At Tuesday's news conference, Pevkur said the drone was shot down shortly after 12:00 local time (09:00 GMT) between the lake of Võrtsjärv and the town of Põltsamaa.

He said the projectile had been identified as a potential threat even before it entered Estonia's air space.

"We received early information from Latvia about a drone that had strayed off course, and Estonia tracked the drone until Romanian fighter jets participating in the Baltic air policing mission shot it down," the Estonian defence ministry said in a statement.

Pevkur added he had "immediately" discussed the incident with his Ukrainian counterpart, who apologised for the incident.

"Estonia has not granted permission to use its airspace to anyone other than its allies, and the Ukrainians have not asked for this permission," the Estonian defence minister said.

Local media outlets later published photos of what they said were drone fragments on the ground.

The drone crashed into a forest, about 30m (98ft) from the nearest residential building, Estonia's ERR public broadcaster reported.

It quoted a local resident as saying: "There was a loud bang and I saw the drone fall from the sky."

In Ukraine, Foreign Ministry spokesman Heorhii Tykhyi said "Russia continues to redirect Ukrainian drones into the Baltics" and did this "on purpose, together with intensified propaganda".

title.en: 'Ebola has tortured us': Fear grips eastern DR Congo as deadly virus spreads
title.zh: “埃博拉折磨着我们”：随着致命病毒的传播，恐惧笼罩刚果民主共和国东部

summary.en: The health minister has acknowledged that medics are playing catch-up with the virus after being slow to detect it.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Fear has gripped Ebola-hit areas in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo as the suspected number of deaths continues to rise, as officials say they are struggling to catch up to an outbreak that may have previously been spreading undetected.

"Ebola has tortured us," says a taxi rider in his late twenties in the gold-mining town of Rwampara.

Following a visit to Ituri province, the epicentre of the outbreak, over the weekend, Congolese Health Minister Dr Samuel Roger Kamba acknowledged health teams are playing catch-up with the virus, which may have been circulating earlier than first detected on 24 April.

The presumed patient zero is a nurse who died in the provincial capital Bunia, but was buried in Mongwalu, also a gold-mining town. Most of the suspected cases and deaths have been reported there and in neighbouring Rwampara.

Rwampara resident Fred Kiza told the BBC that "there is fear", which he calls "normal when there's a disease like this."

As of Tuesday, there were 514 suspected cases, with 136 people believed to have died from the virus, officials said. One person has also died in neighbouring Uganda.

Cases have also been identified in Butembo city and rebel-controlled Goma in North Kivu province, as well as in South Kivu province.

Health officials say that several deaths occurred in the community without being reported to the authorities, meaning they could not be investigated at the time.

According to the health ministry, formal community alerts were only registered from 8 May.

"At community level, this hasn't been effective," Dr Kamba explained. "It means someone may have died before him [the presumed index case], or someone else may have been sick before him, but no one reported it."

He added: "We really need to look within the community to understand what happened - how people became ill and sometimes even died without any report being filed."

The outbreak has been caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola. DR Congo - which is currently facing its 17th outbreak of Ebola - is more familiar with the Zaïre species.

Bundibugyo has caused only two outbreaks before - in 2007 and 2012 - where it killed around 30% of people infected.

Dr Kamba explained the symptoms: "There is heavy bleeding everywhere, very high fever. But Bundibugyo can show fewer obvious signs, which delays diagnosis because people think, 'No, this is just malaria.'"

In Mongwalu, some deaths were attributed not to illness, but to witchcraft. The belief became known locally as the "coffin phenomenon" - the idea that anyone who touched the coffin of a deceased person would also die.

title.en: Hungary's new Prime Minister Magyar seeks to fix Poland ties
title.zh: 匈牙利新总理马扎尔寻求修复波兰关系

summary.en: Peter Magyar hopes to mend relations with Poland during his first state visit to Warsaw. What lessons could he learn from Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Peter Magyar hopes to mend relations with Poland during his first state visit to Warsaw. What lessons could he learn from Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk?

Peter Magyar's center-right Tisza Party won the parliamentary election in Hungary on April 12, 2026 — and Polish liberals were thrilled. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote on X, "Welcome back to Europe." He also posted a video showing him on the phone with election winner Magyar during a visit to South Korea . "I think I'm even happier than you are," Tusk enthused at the time.

On Tuesday, ten days after his inauguration  on May 9, 2026, Magyar's first trip abroad took him to Poland , "our natural allies," as Hungary's new leader called the Poles last year.

Historically, Poland and Hungary  have mostly had close ties. Under the Polish right-wing nationalist governments of the Law and Justice Party ( PiS , 2015–2023) and the Hungarian Civic Alliance (Fidesz, 2010–2026), Warsaw and Budapest formed an illiberal, EU-critical alliance for years. However, this rapport was increasingly put under pressure, particularly since the start of the war in Ukraine. The pro-Russian policies of Hungary's long-time Prime Minister Viktor Orban were never supported by the Polish right-wing party.

In late 2023, when Tusk's pro-European center-left government took the helm in Poland, relations hit rock bottom. "Everything is clear between us, we have different views on every matter, on every issue," Tusk told Polish reporters in October 2025. He added that Orban opposed democratic norms and judicial transparency.

Relations between Budapest and Warsaw cooled further when Hungary granted political asylum to Poland's former Minister of Justice, Zbigniew Ziobro, and his deputy, Marcin Romanowski, following Tusk's election victory. Both politicians are under investigation at home on suspicion of corruption . The new Hungarian prime minister, however, wants to mend Polish-Hungarian relations and present himself as a reliable, pro-European partner.

Magyar's visit to Poland is "symbolic" says Marcin Bosacki, State Secretary at the Polish Ministry of Foreign Affairs. "It is important to us that the new Hungarian government is demonstrating, through such a powerful symbolic gesture, that friendship with Poland is important."

Expectations for the meeting are high on both sides, sociologist Edit Zgut-Przybylska, a researcher at the Polish Academy of Sciences in Warsaw and at the CEU Democracy Institute in Budapest, told DW. "The trust that was destroyed by the pro-Russian and extremely anti-European policies of the former Hungarian government must be restored," she said.

title.en: Rising Cuba-US tensions amid talk of drones, emergency plans
title.zh: 无人机和紧急计划的讨论加剧了古巴与美国的紧张关系

summary.en: Cuba’s reported purchase of drones and renewed threats with the US are stoking fears of escalation. Amid blackouts and shortages, many Cubans expressed outrage at official advice to prepare for potential attack.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Cuba’s reported purchase of drones and renewed threats with the US are stoking fears of escalation. Amid blackouts and shortages, many Cubans expressed outrage at official advice to prepare for potential attack.

"This is a joke. If we’re living hand-to-mouth, how can we save food for the war?" wrote a Cuban social media user after the publication of an official guide with recommendations on how to prepare for a potential military attack by the United States .

This and other outraged messages reflect the confusion and unease felt by many Cubans following the guidelines released in recent days by Cuba’s Civil Defense, amid growing tension between Havana and Washington.

The "Family Guide for the Protection of the Population in the Event of Military Aggression" recommends packing a backpack with personal documents, a radio, a flashlight, matches, candles, a first-aid kit, food for three days, drinking water, personal hygiene items as well as medications for chronic illnesses. It also suggests identifying shelters that can be used in the event of an airstrike.

The publication of the guidelines comes at one of the most tense moments in decades for the already strained Cuban-US relations. In recent weeks, US president  Donald Trump has repeatedly hinted at taking action against Cuba , going so far as to say that "Cuba is next."

Tensions escalated further after the US media outlet Axios quoted intelligence sources as saying that Cuba had acquired more than 300 military drones and was evaluating possible scenarios for their use near the US base at Guantanamo.

However, analyst Guadalupe Correa-Cabrera, said that the limited number of drones would not pose a significant threat. "In military and strategic terms, 300 drones are nothing compared to the capacity of the United States," Correa-Cabrera, a professor of Politics and Government at George Mason University in Virginia, told DW. "The asymmetries are enormous."

The expert believes that the current situation must be viewed in a broader geopolitical context, marked by tensions between Washington and other global powers such as Russia and China. "Cuba’s geographical location, beyond its symbolic significance, is fundamental for any country that seeks to control the Western Hemisphere," she explains.

According to Correa-Cabrera, it is not only the drones that are a cause for concern, but also Havana’s potential strategic alliances with countries hostile to the United States and the role that new forms of "irregular warfare" could play.

"We are not talking about a war between Cuba and the United States, but rather a global conflict involving other nations," she explained.

title.en: NATO planes down suspected Ukrainian drone over Estonia
title.zh: 北约飞机在爱沙尼亚上空击落疑似乌克兰无人机

summary.en: A NATO military jet has shot down a suspected Ukrainian drone in Estonian airspace. As Ukraine targets Russia's Baltic oil facilities more often and more intensely, more such drones are straying into allies' territory.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 一架北约军用飞机在爱沙尼亚领空击落了一架疑似乌克兰无人机。随着乌克兰更频繁、更强烈地攻击俄罗斯波罗的海石油设施，越来越多的此类无人机误入盟国领土。 北约周二证实，驻立陶宛波罗的海空中警察部队的一架 F16 喷气式飞机在爱沙尼亚领空击落了一架无人机。 爱沙尼亚和拉脱维亚都发布了空中警报威胁，报告称其领空有无人机。目前尚不清楚他们指的是同一架飞机还是不同的飞机。 爱沙尼亚军方表示，一架无人机于当地时间周二中午（格林威治标准时间 0900）左右进入该国领空，从俄罗斯进入该国东南部地区。 当地时间12时14分，它在一次训练飞行中被一架罗马尼亚北约战斗机用一枚导弹击落。 军方表示：“这起事件是在俄罗斯实施包括 GPS 欺骗和干扰在内的激烈电子战的情况下发生的。” 军方表示，在这架无人机进入其领空之前，他们一直在对其进行监视，并称击落它的决定是为了“尽量减少对平民和基础设施的影响”。 北约后来证实，它在爱沙尼亚领空击落了一架无人机，并表示调查正在进行中，北约“已准备好并能够对任何潜在的空中威胁做出反应”。 周二的事件是最近几周该地区发生的一系列侵犯领空事件中的最新一起，俄罗斯在波罗的海的设施，尤其是滨海边疆区和乌斯季卢加的主要石油设施遭受的袭击不断加剧。 从乌克兰到这些地点的飞行路线靠近立陶宛、拉脱维亚、爱沙尼亚和芬兰等波罗的海北约成员国的边界，而无人机防御系统可能会干扰飞机的导航。 波罗的海国家在公开回应中广泛指责俄罗斯，称乌克兰有正当理由攻击俄罗斯境内的地点，作为其防御战争的一部分。 “这些事件是俄罗斯战争和挑衅的直接结果。爱沙尼亚正在加强与乌克兰的合作，以增强我们的防空和反无人机能力，”爱沙尼亚外交部长马古斯·查克纳在网上发帖称。 这个问题在本月在拉脱维亚尤其达到了紧要关头，联合政府因该国处理降落在其领土上的流浪无人机的方式发生内部争论而垮台。 总理埃维卡·西利纳 (Evika Silina) 解雇了国防部长，随后在失去联盟伙伴并因此失去多数席位后很快不得不辞职。 5 月 15 日，芬兰，无人机活动警告导致赫尔辛基国际机场和附近其他地区出现混乱。

title.en: China's zero-tariff for Africa: Win-win or winner takes all?
title.zh: 中国对非洲零关税：双赢还是赢家通吃？

summary.en: China has opened its market to 53 African countries, calling it a “golden key” to prosperity. But while new opportunities emerge, analysts warn the reality for African economies is more complex.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
China has opened its market to 53 African countries, calling it a “golden key” to prosperity. But while new opportunities emerge, analysts warn the reality for African economies is more complex.

The first shipments of avocados from Kenya  arrived in China under Beijing's new zero-tariff rule early this month. A clear sign, analysts say, that the deal is starting to have real effects.

The policy, which came into effect on May 1, gives Africa's biggest economies tariff-free access to China's market for the next two years. 

"China introducing the zero tariff is very very encouraging," Olive Gichuri, a Kenyan coffee farmer, told DW. "It means better earnings for the farmers. When our coffee becomes very competitive, it means more demand and also more market for farmers."

"They [farmers] are not only limited to selling their products in the local [Kenyan] market," Gichuri said, adding that the zero tariff had opened the market in China.

Lauren Johnston, a senior research fellow and international economist specializing in China, Africa and geoeconomics at the AustChina Institute in Melbourne, told DW that the policy "is actually a gift mainly to Africa's stronger economies that are middle-income countries and that are sort of well-positioned to elevate exports." 

In 2025, China and Africa traded a record $348 billion (€312 billion) in goods, according to China's General Administration of Customs. China has been Africa's biggest trading partner for 16 consecutive years .

African countries sent about $123 billion worth of goods to China, mostly oil, minerals, and other raw materials . In return, they bought around $225 billion worth of products from China, mainly manufactured goods, electronics, vehicles, and machinery.

Africa's trade deficit with China grew sharply, hitting a record $102 billion in 2025 , up from roughly $62 billion the previous year, according to official Chinese data.

"The export price is low because we do not add value to our exports," Adu Owusu Sarkodie, an economist and senior lecturer at the University of Ghana, told DW. "The best way to position ourselves is to get a value addition to our exports, so that we can earn a higher price, higher income, and then reduce poverty."

Much of this increase in the deficit stems from China's push to diversify its supply chains amid its trade dispute with the United States . Africa's growing demand for green technologies such as electric vehicles, motorbikes, and solar panels has also led to increased imports from China.

Kenya is among the clearest early beneficiaries. China granted about 98.2% zero‑duty market access to Kenyan products under the  Early Harvest Agreement .

title.en: Families 'terrified' for Australians on Gaza flotilla detained by Israel
title.zh: 家人对被以色列拘留的加沙船队中的澳大利亚人感到“恐惧”

summary.en: The wellbeing of 11 Australian activists is unknown after their Gaza-bound flotilla was intercepted overnight.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Australian government is urgently seeking information on the whereabouts and condition of 11 Australian activists allegedly detained by Israel after boats in a Gaza-bound aid flotilla were intercepted by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) in international waters.

The location and condition of the Australians remains unknown, and the flotilla's media delegate confirmed there had been no contact with the activists since the delegation was intercepted.

The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) said it was urgently seeking confirmation of the welfare of Australians it believed to be detained.

"We will continue to make clear our expectation that any detainees receive humane treatment in line with international norms," a DFAT spokesperson said on Tuesday.

Flotilla organisers identified the Australian activists as Anny Mokotow, Bianca Webb-Pullman, Neve O'Connor, Violet Coco, Gemma O'Toole, Sam Woripa Watson, Zack Schofield, Helen O'Sullivan, Juliet Lamont, Isla Lamont and Surya McEwen.

The Israeli foreign ministry said in a post on X that activists from the "provocation flotilla" had been transferred to Israeli vessels and claimed that no aid had been found on their boats.

The missing Australians' parents and loved ones called for immediate government action at a conference at the State Library Victoria on Tuesday.

Julie Webb-Pullman, the mother of general practitioner Bianca Webb-Pullman, said she hadn't heard from her daughter since 8.09pm on Monday, as the flotilla was intercepted.

"Serial kidnappers have done it again, abducted my daughter in international waters while she was delivering humanitarian aid," she told reporters.

"Yet our pathetic prime minister cannot even rustle up a condemnation, let alone demand accountability."

Susie O'Toole said she hadn't had any direct contact with her 23-year-old daughter, Gemma, and assumed the cohort was on a prison cargo ship bound for Ashdod prison in Israel.

"Most probably they've been left out in the sun like most people previously have been, held in stress positions, not given water, not given food," she said.

"We are terrified about Gemma's wellbeing. We demand the Australian government do everything they can to get her home safely."

title.en: Three people killed in San Diego mosque shooting, two suspected gunmen found dead
title.zh: 圣地亚哥清真寺枪击案致三人死亡，两名嫌疑枪手被发现死亡

summary.en: Authorities are investigating a shooting at an Islamic center in San Diego that killed three people as a hate crime, with two suspected gunmen found dead. The FBI has been called in.
summary.zh: 圣地亚哥一处伊斯兰中心发生枪击案，造成三人死亡，两名嫌疑枪手被发现死亡。当局正将此案作为仇恨犯罪进行调查，联邦调查局已介入。

body.en:
A shooting at a mosque complex in California killed three people on Tuesday AEST, with two suspected teenage gunmen later found dead in a car from self-inflicted gunshot wounds, police said.

Police said emergency response teams found the victims outside the sprawling Islamic Center of San Diego, before later finding the alleged shooters, aged 18 and 17, also dead. Police originally gave the elder shooter's age as 19.

TV footage from a helicopter showed armed response teams gathered outside a building, with one unidentified person lying in a pool of blood.

Dozens of patrol cars were lined up around the Islamic Center, described on its website as the largest mosque in San Diego county, which lies in southern California.

After a short period of lockdown when authorities advised residents to stay inside, San Diego police announced that the threat at the centre had been "neutralised".

"We received a call of an active shooter at the Islamic centre. Within four minutes, officers arrived on scene and observed immediately three deceased victims out in front," San Diego police chief Scott Wahl told reporters.

"We immediately began to deploy with an active shooter response into the mosque and adjacent school," he said, adding that police had received calls about more gunfire nearby, where a landscaper at work had been shot at but not hit.

All of the children who were attending a day school that is part of the mosque complex were accounted for and safe after the shooting, Wahl said.

He said the FBI was called in to assist in the investigation of the incident, which the police chief said authorities were treating as a hate crime.

Wahl said the mother of one of the two suspects had called police about two hours before the shooting to report that her son, whom she described as suicidal, had run away from home taking three guns she owned and her vehicle.

According to the chief, the mother said her son was with a companion and the two were dressed in camouflage.

Police initiated efforts to track down the youths and were dispatching patrols to a nearby shopping mall and the son's high school as a precaution when calls came in reporting the mosque shooting.

Outside the Islamic centre, police found a vehicle in the middle of the street with the alleged shooters dead inside.

"The suspects at this point appear to have died from self-inflicted gunshot wounds. There were no officers involved in firing their weapons," Wahl said.

Police said that a security guard at the Islamic centre was among the three victims killed. The identity of the other two fatalities was not immediately clear.

Officials credited the slain security guard as likely having helped prevent further bloodshed.

body.zh: 警方称，澳大利亚东部标准时间周二，加利福尼亚州一座清真寺发生枪击事件，造成三人死亡，随后发现两名疑似青少年枪手因自伤枪伤死在一辆汽车中。 警方表示，应急响应小组在圣地亚哥庞大的伊斯兰中心外发现了受害者，随后发现分别为 19 岁和 17 岁的涉嫌枪击者也已死亡。 直升机的电视画面显示，武装反应小组聚集在一座建筑物外，一名身份不明的人躺在血泊中。 数十辆巡逻车在伊斯兰中心周围排队，该中心在其网站上被描述为位于南加州圣地亚哥县最大的清真寺。 在当局建议居民呆在室内的短暂封锁之后，圣地亚哥警方宣布该中心的威胁已“消除”。 圣地亚哥警察局长斯科特·瓦尔告诉记者：“我们接到伊斯兰中心一名枪手的电话。四分钟内，警察赶到现场，立即发现前面有三名遇难者。” 他说：“我们立即开始向清真寺和附近的学校部署积极的枪手应对措施。”他补充说，警方接到电话称附近发生更多枪击事件，一名正在工作的园艺师遭到枪击，但没有击中。 瓦尔说，枪击事件发生后，所有在清真寺建筑群内的走读学校上学的孩子都已找到并安全。 他说，联邦调查局被召来协助调查这起事件，警察局长表示，当局将这起事件视为仇恨犯罪。 在伊斯兰中心外，警方在街道中央发现一辆汽车，据称枪手死在车内。 瓦尔说：“目前嫌疑人似乎是死于自伤枪伤。没有警察参与开枪。” 警方称，遇难的三名受害者包括伊斯兰中心的一名保安。另外两名死者的身份尚不清楚。 清真寺伊玛目塔哈·哈桑表示，清真寺内所有工作人员、教师和儿童都很安全。 “我们以前从未经历过这样的悲剧。此时此刻我所能说的就是祈祷并与我们社区的所有家庭站在一起，”他说。 他告诉记者：“我已经得到了一些早期的最新消息，但我们将回去认真研究。” 州长加文·纽瑟姆新闻办公室表示，他已听取了有关此次明显袭击事件的简报。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

body.en: Tim Rood and Phil Coughlin on Xi Jinping’s reference to the Thucydides trap in a meeting with Donald Trump In explaining Xi Jinping’s allusion to the Thucydides trap, Kate Lamb refers to Thucydides’ statement that “it was the rise of Athens and the fear that this instilled in Sparta that made war inevitable” ( What is the Thucydides Trap and why did Xi Jinping mention it in his meeting with Donald Trump?, 15 May ). That is the translation used by the Harvard political scientist Graham Allison, who popularised the phrase “Thucydides trap”, and who attributes the translation to Richard Crawley’s 1874 edition. It is often said that Thucydides’ Greek is better translated as “the Athenians growing great and creating fear in the Spartans compelled them towards making war”. Russia’s president is in Beijing for a meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, only days after a visit by Donald Trump. Follow DW for more.

Russia continues to tout its so‑called “no‑limits” partnership with China, but new figures suggest the relationship is becoming increasingly one‑sided.

Trade between the two eased last year due to lower oil prices, yet Russian exports to China have nearly doubled since the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

DW examines how China’s trade ties and financial backing are helping to sustain Russia’s economy .

Ahead of the talks in Beijing, the Kremlin said that Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping would sign a statement on building a "multipolar" world order, among many other documents.

Some 40 documents are to be signed in total, Kremlin foreign policy advisor Yuri Ushakov said, including bilateral agreements touching on industry, trade, transport and construction.

The two leaders are to conduct informal talks "over tea", Ushakov said, where they are expected to discuss the conflicts in Iran and Ukraine and other issues.

Beijing has repeatedly called for Western states to abandon what it describes as "Cold War mentality" and accept China's role in an increasingly multipolar world.

Russian President Vladimir Putin has arrived in China for talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

The Russian president landed at Beijing Capital International Airport shortly after 11:15 p.m. (0315 UTC).

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Berlin hopes that Chinese leader Xi Jinping will use his influence on Russian President Vladimir Putin to urge him to end Moscow's invasion of Ukraine.

"We do not expect a fundamental shift in the strategic relations between Russia and China at this stage," Merz was cited by German news agency DPA as saying.

"But we naturally associate this visit with the hope that President Xi will also urge President Putin to end this war in Ukraine, which he cannot win," he said, pointing to reportedly high casualty rates among Russian soldiers.

Russia has become increasingly reliant on its links to China's economy after being isolated from Western countries due to its war in Ukraine.

China has not condemned the Russian invasion and has called for a negotiated settlement between Kyiv and Moscow .

Russian President Vladimir Putin was on his way to Beijing on Tuesday for talks with Chinese President   Xi Jinping .

The Kremlin said that Putin and Xi were to discuss ways to "further strengthen" Russian-Chinese ties and "exchange views on key international and regional issues."

In such high-stakes diplomacy, the need for profound wisdom is evident. James 1:5 reminds us that wisdom is available to all who ask God for it, a principle vital for those navigating complex international relations.
reflection.zh: 当大国领导人会晤时，他们的决定对全球稳定和数百万人的福祉具有举足轻重的影响。在这种高风险的外交中，对深刻智慧的需求显而易见。雅各书1:5提醒我们，凡向雅伟祈求智慧的，雅伟必厚赐于他，这对于那些处理复杂国际关系的人来说是至关重要的原则。

verse.textEn: If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault.
verse.textZh: 你们中间若有缺少智慧的，应当求那厚赐与众人、也不斥责人的神，主就必赐给他。

title.en: Fears of new China shock as EU industry’s reliance on imports grows
title.zh: 欧盟工业对进口依赖加剧，引发对新一轮中国冲击的担忧

summary.en: European trade analysts are warning of a potential "China shock" as the continent's industries become increasingly reliant on imported components from China. Concerns are rising that this dependency could lead to the decline of local factories and job losses, effectively undermining European industrial autonomy.
summary.zh: 欧洲贸易分析师警告称，随着欧洲工业对中国进口零部件的依赖日益增长，可能会出现新的“中国冲击”。人们担心这种依赖可能导致本地工厂衰落和失业，从而实际上削弱欧洲的工业自主权。

body.en: Rising volume of components imported from China prompts warning of cannibalisation of European industries Europe is facing a fresh China shock that threatens to cannibalise local factories, leading to job losses and de facto colonisation of industry by Beijing, trade analysts and representatives have said. They fear the plunging exchange rate and support for Chinese “zombie firms” has echoes of the crisis in the US 25 years ago when the term “China shock” was coined. It referred to the impact of China bursting on to the global trade stage after becoming a member of the World Trade Organization, with soaring imports displacing local industries and causing the loss of up to 2.5m jobs. Proverbs reminds us that wisdom involves seeing danger ahead and taking prudent steps, rather than ignoring risks that could lead to hardship. This calls for careful consideration of long-term...
reflection.zh: 贸易分析师的警告突显了经济政策中远见的重要性，敦促领导者在潜在脆弱性升级之前予以识别。箴言提醒我们，智慧在于预见危险并采取审慎的措施，而不是忽视可能导致困境的风险。这要求在国家和国际经济决策中仔细考虑长远后果。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: Trump told Taiwan not to 'go independent' - but does it want to?
title.zh: 特朗普告诉台湾不要“独立”——但它想独立吗？

summary.en: Taiwan independence is the reddest of red lines for China, which claims the island as its own.
summary.zh: 台湾独立是中国最敏感的红线，中国声称该岛是其领土。

body.en:
Hours after meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing last week, Donald Trump issued a stern warning to Taiwan against pursuing independence.

"I'm not looking to have somebody go independent. And, you know, we're supposed to travel 9,500 miles to fight a war. I'm not looking for that. I want them to cool down. I want China to cool down," he told Fox News in an interview that aired on Friday.

Trump's comments - some of the strongest a US president has made so far on the issue - immediately sparked a flurry of responses from Taiwan saying it does not see the need to formally declare independence.

Taiwanese independence is the reddest of red lines for Beijing, which claims Taiwan as its own and has accused its president Lai Ching-te of being a separatist.

It dates back to the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949, when the Chinese Communist Party won control of China and the losing Kuomintang forces retreated to Taiwan, relocating its government to Taipei.

Beijing has since claimed the self-governed island. But after Xi came to power, the Chinese government has doubled down on its threats and sought ways to stamp out what it sees as separatism. Taiwan's "reunification" with China has become a key goal - Xi himself has called it an "unstoppable" reality.

In recent years, China has stepped up various forms of pressure, through military drills that have simulated blockades; the diplomatic isolation of Taiwan; and greyzone warfare where it sends warships and fighter jets close to Taiwanese waters and airspace on a regular basis.

During last week's summit, Xi had told Trump that the issue of Taiwan was the most important one in US-China relations, and that mishandling it could lead to conflict.

As the US is Taiwan's closest ally - it is bound by law to provide the island with the means to defend itself - observers have long worried that any attack on Taiwan would draw the US into direct conflict with China.

China has made clear its stance on Taiwan in its Anti-Secession Law, introduced in 2005, in which it states that it wants "peaceful reunification" with the island.

But the Anti-Secession Law also states that should "Taiwan independence" forces cause secession from China, or the possibility of "peaceful reunification" has been exhausted, China can employ "non-peaceful means" to protect its territorial integrity.

What this means is that China does not rule out the use of military force to take Taiwan if it deems it necessary. Most people believe that a formal declaration of independence by Taiwan's government would trigger this response.

Taiwan has close economic and cultural ties with China. But most people in Taiwan, which has a robust democratic system, see themselves as politically distinct from China, which has become increasingly...
body.zh: 上周在北京会见中国国家主席习近平几小时后，唐纳德·特朗普向台湾发出严厉警告，不要追求独立。 “我不希望有人独立。而且，你知道，我们应该行驶 9,500 英里去打一场战争。我不是在寻找那样的结果。我希望他们冷静下来。我希望中国冷静下来，”他在周五播出的福克斯新闻采访中说道。 特朗普的言论是迄今为止美国总统在这个问题上发表的最强烈的言论之一，立即引发了台湾的一系列反应，称台湾认为没有必要正式宣布独立。 台独是北京最红的红线，北京宣称台湾是自己的，并指责台湾总统赖清德是分裂分子。 这可以追溯到1949年中国内战结束时，当时中国共产党控制了中国，失败的国民党军队撤退到台湾，政府迁往台北。 此后，北京宣称对该岛拥有主权。但习近平上台后，中国政府加大了威胁力度，并寻求消除其眼中的分裂主义的方法。台湾与中国的“统一”已成为一个关键目标——习近平本人称其为“不可阻挡”的现实。 近年来，中国通过军事演习、模拟封锁等方式加大了各种形式的压力；对台湾的外交孤立；以及灰色地带战，定期派遣军舰和战斗机接近台湾海域和空域。 在上周的峰会上，习近平告诉特朗普，台湾问题是美中关系中最重要的问题，处理不当可能会导致冲突。 由于美国是台湾最亲密的盟友——它有法律义务向台湾提供自卫手段——观察人士长期以来一直担心对台湾的任何攻击都会使美国陷入与中国的直接冲突。 中国在2005年出台的《反分裂国家法》中明确表明了其对台湾的立场，其中表示希望与台湾“和平统一”。 但《反分裂国家法》也规定，如果“台独”势力从中国分裂出去，或者“和平统一”的可能性已经耗尽，中国可以采取“非和平方式”维护领土完整。 这意味着，如果中国认为有必要，不排除使用武力收复台湾。大多数人认为，台湾政府正式宣布独立就会引发这种反应。 台湾与中国有着密切的经济和文化联系。但拥有健全民主制度的台湾，大多数人认为自己在政治上与中国截然不同，而中国已变得越来越……

reflection.en: This story highlights the deep-seated geopolitical tensions surrounding Taiwan's status, where fundamental disagreements could lead to conflict. Romans 12:18 encourages us to live at peace with everyone, as far as it depends on us. In complex international relations, this principle calls all parties to diligently seek peaceful coexistence, even amidst...
reflection.zh: 这个故事凸显了围绕台湾地位的根深蒂固的地缘政治紧张局势，其中根本性的分歧可能导致冲突。罗马书12:18鼓励我们，若是可能，总要尽力与众人和睦。在复杂的国际关系中，这一原则呼吁所有各方，即使面对深刻而严峻的分歧，也要努力寻求和平共处。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: What really holds China and Russia together
title.zh: 是什么真正将中国和俄罗斯联系在一起

summary.en: The relationship endures despite a power imbalance, with both sides recognising that it is too important to fail.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
As they strolled through Tiananmen Square in Beijing last September, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin appeared to muse over the possibility that organ transplants could dramatically extend human life.

"Human organs can be continuously transplanted. The longer you live, the younger you become, and even achieve immortality", Putin's interpreter was heard saying.

"Some predict that in this century, humans may live up to 150 years old," Xi's interpreter was heard responding.

It was a fitting conversation for two strongmen, who have described each other as best friends, and who, after a combined 39 years in power, show no signs of stepping down.

This was a rare insight into what is quite a misunderstood partnership. This scrap of unscripted conversation is one of the few glimpses into a highly secretive relationship.

Putin will be returning to Beijing this week, coinciding with the 25th anniversary of the Treaty of Good-Neighbourliness and Friendly Cooperation between Russia and China.

When US President Donald Trump visited Xi last week he was met with an extravaganza of banquets with gold tableware and a visit to an ancient temple. Putin's visit feels far more low-key, with little information released in advance.

The Kremlin's spokesperson said they hoped to hear first-hand information about the Trump-Xi meeting.

Xi reportedly name-dropped his friend Putin to Trump last week, when the two leaders walked through Zhongnanhai, which is normally off-limits to foreign visitors, joking about how Putin had visited Beijing's political sanctuary before.

While some in Washington may have been hoping that Trump could wean Beijing off Moscow, such hopes appear little more than wishful thinking.

China and Russia have in recent years described their ties as a "friendship with no limits". So, what is this based on, and will their love affair last?

The relationship is highly uneven, and any deals struck between the two countries will likely be on Chinese terms, says Alexander Gabuev, director of the Carnegie Russia Eurasia Center think tank. He stresses, "Russia is fully in China's pocket, and China can dictate the terms."

This dynamic persists across many sectors, not least the economy. China is Russia's largest trading partner, while Russia makes up just 4% of China's international trade. China exports more than any other country to Russia, and its economy is significantly larger than Russia's.

Years of western sanctions have gradually pushed Moscow deeper into trade engagement with Beijing. Tech giant Huawei, which was sanctioned by the US and also forced out of UK 5G networks following a review by the British government, has capitalised on the lack of Western companies to become a key pillar of Russia's...
body.zh: 去年九月，当中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京漫步在北京天安门广场时，他们似乎在思考器官移植可以大幅延长人类寿命的可能性。 普京的翻译说：“人体器官可以不断移植。你活得越久，你就越年轻，甚至可以达到永生”。 “有人预测，本世纪，人类可能活到150岁，”习近平的翻译回答道。 对于两位强人来说，这是一次恰如其分的对话，他们称对方为最好的朋友，并且在执政 39 年后，没有表现出下台的迹象。 这是对一种被严重误解的伙伴关系的罕见洞察。这段即兴对话是为数不多的一段高度秘密关系的一瞥。 普京将于本周返回北京，恰逢俄中睦邻友好合作条约签署25周年。 当美国总统唐纳德·特朗普上周访问习近平时，他受到了盛大的宴会和金餐具的欢迎，并参观了一座古老的寺庙。普京的访问感觉要低调得多，事先几乎没有发布任何信息。 克里姆林宫发言人表示，希望听到有关特习会的第一手信息。 据报道，上周，当两位领导人走过通常禁止外国游客进入的中南海时，习近平向特朗普点名了他的朋友普京，并开玩笑说普京以前曾访问过北京的政治庇护所。 尽管华盛顿的一些人可能希望特朗普能够让北京摆脱莫斯科的影响，但这种希望似乎只不过是一厢情愿。 近年来，中国和俄罗斯将两国关系描述为“无限的友谊”。那么，这是基于什么，他们的恋情会持续下去吗？ 卡内基俄罗斯欧亚中心智库主任亚历山大·加布耶夫表示，两国关系极不平衡，两国之间达成的任何协议都可能按照中国的条件进行。他强调，“俄罗斯完全在中国的口袋里，中国可以决定条款。” 这种动态在许多领域持续存在，尤其是经济领域。中国是俄罗斯最大的贸易伙伴，而俄罗斯仅占中国国际贸易的4%。中国对俄罗斯的出口超过任何其他国家，其经济规模也明显大于俄罗斯。 多年的西方制裁逐渐促使莫斯科加深与北京的贸易接触。科技巨头华为受到美国制裁，并在英国政府审查后被迫退出英国 5G 网络，该公司利用西方公司的缺乏，成为俄罗斯的关键支柱。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: Australia orders firms to sell stakes in rare earths miner
title.zh: 澳大利亚命令公司出售稀土矿商股份

summary.en: Australia's treasurer ordered China-linked companies to divest their stakes in Northern Minerals, a rare earths miner, citing the need to protect Australia's national interests.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚财政部长命令与中国有关联的公司剥离其在稀土矿商北方矿业的股份，理由是需要保护澳大利亚的国家利益。

body.zh: 财政部长命令与中国有联系的公司剥离北方矿业公司以保护澳大利亚的利益。 澳大利亚命令与中国有关的股东出售其在正在开发稀土矿的北方矿业公司的股份。 财务主管吉姆·查尔默斯 (Jim Chalmers) 表示，由于担心中国投资者试图控制北方矿产公司，他已于周一发布了命令。 这家总部位于澳大利亚的矿业公司正在西澳大利亚州最北部开发布朗斯山脉项目，以开采大量的镝和铽储量。 查尔默在一份声明中表示，他的决定旨在保护该国的国家利益并确保遵守其外国投资框架。 他说：“我们运营着一个强大且非歧视性的外国投资框架，如果需要，我们将采取进一步行动，以保护我们与此事相关的国家利益。” 镝和铽是对于耐热高性能磁体至关重要的重稀土元素。这些产品用于清洁能源应用，例如混合动力汽车和风力涡轮机，以及专业国防应用。 它开采约 60% 的原材料，并精炼约占全球供应量的 95%-98%。这使其几乎垄断了加工商业镝。 北方矿业公司的稀土预计将在澳大利亚新建的炼油厂进行加工。 当这两个项目上线时，澳大利亚将成为第一个重要的非中国加工镝来源国。 包括澳大利亚和美国在内的西方国家正在寻求限制中国对关键矿产的投资。 近年来，中国投资者一直寻求在北方矿业公司持有大量股份。 关于查尔默最近的处置令，六名股东中有三名的地址在中国，两名在香港，一名在英属维尔京群岛上市。 但早在 2024 年，澳大利亚就已经利用外国收购法迫使五名投资者出售其在北方矿业公司的股份。 2025 年，财政部采取了史无前例的举措，将最大股东之一告上法庭，称其藐视出售令，而是将股份转入其自己董事的名下。

reflection.en: Nations, like individuals, often face complex decisions to safeguard their future and resources. This action by Australia's treasurer reflects a strategic move to protect perceived national interests in a critical industry. Proverbs 27:12 reminds us of the wisdom in foreseeing potential challenges and taking prudent steps to secure what is vital.
reflection.zh: 国家如同个人，常需作出复杂决定以保障其未来和资源。澳大利亚财政部长的这一举动，反映了在关键产业中保护国家利益的战略考量。箴言27:12提醒我们，预见潜在挑战并采取审慎措施来维护重要事物，是明智之举。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: EV battery supply chains in focus as China halts sulphuric acid exports
title.zh: 中国暂停硫酸出口，电动汽车电池供应链受关注

summary.en: China's decision to stop exporting sulphuric acid is expected to create pressure on global supply chains for both electric vehicle batteries and fertilizers.
summary.zh: 中国停止出口硫酸预计将对电动汽车电池和化肥的全球供应链造成压力。

body.en:
China has banned exports of sulphuric acid, the world's most used industrial chemical and a crucial ingredient in battery and clothing manufacturing, as well as fertiliser production and metal processing industries.

The move comes amid pressures on supply of the chemical after conflict in the Middle East disrupted sulphur shipments through the Strait of Hormuz earlier this year.

Marina Zhang from the University of Technology Sydney's Australia-China Relations Institute said that, while the ban may have been presented by China as temporary, it signals a policy shift from Australia's largest trading partner towards increasingly prioritising control over industrial inputs.

"It's not just finished products, but the upstream materials, processing technologies and basic industrial ingredients that allow advanced manufacturing to scale … So while the immediate measure may be temporary, the underlying logic is structural," Zhang told SBS News.

Sulphur is the primary ingredient used to produce sulphuric acid, meaning shipping and processing delays of the raw material in the Gulf region have created flow-on effects for manufacturers reliant on a steady supply.

In 2025, about half of the global seaborne supply of sulphur came from the Middle East.

China accounted for a significant share of sulphuric acid shipments from Asia last year and remains one of the world's largest exporters. The loss of that supply is now raising concerns among overseas buyers already scrambling to secure alternative sources.

While the impacts are expected to be spread across multiple industries, analysts say battery supply chains could be among the most exposed.

Zhang said the situation "reveals a paradox at the heart of the clean-energy transition … which depends on minerals that require very energy-intensive, chemical-intensive and often environmentally difficult processing".

"Yet many Western countries have spent decades outsourcing precisely those 'dirty' industrial activities."

Sulphuric acid also plays an important role in processing metals such as nickel and copper, both used extensively in electric vehicle batteries and energy storage systems.

Indonesia's rapidly expanding nickel-processing industry is considered particularly vulnerable to the bans.

The country has become a major producer of battery-grade nickel used in global electric vehicle (EV) supply chains, including by manufacturers linked to Chinese battery maker CATL.

Refining lower-grade nickel ores into battery materials requires large volumes of sulphuric acid for a process known as high-pressure acid leaching.

If supplies remain constrained, refiners could face higher production costs, delays and increased competition for feedstock, potentially flowing through to battery makers and EV...
body.zh: 中国已禁止出口硫酸，硫酸是世界上使用最广泛的工业化学品，也是电池和服装制造、化肥生产和金属加工业的关键成分。 今年早些时候，中东冲突扰乱了通过霍尔木兹海峡的硫磺运输，导致化学品供应面临压力。 悉尼科技大学澳中关系研究所的玛丽娜·张表示，虽然中国提出的禁令可能是暂时的，但它标志着澳大利亚最大贸易伙伴的政策转变，越来越优先考虑对工业投入的控制。 “这不仅仅是成品，还有上游材料、加工技术和基本工业原料，使先进制造业能够规模化……因此，虽然眼前的措施可能是暂时的，但潜在的逻辑是结构性的，”张告诉SBS新闻。 硫是用于生产硫酸的主要成分，这意味着海湾地区原材料的运输和加工延迟对依赖稳定供应的制造商产生了连锁效应。 到 2025 年，全球海运硫磺供应量的一半左右来自中东。 去年，中国占亚洲硫酸出口量的很大一部分，并且仍然是世界最大的出口国之一。这种供应的损失现在引起了已经在争相寻找替代来源的海外买家的担忧。 虽然预计影响将波及多个行业，但分析师表示，电池供应链可能是受影响最大的行业之一。 张说，这种情况“揭示了清洁能源转型核心的一个悖论……这取决于需要能源密集型、化学密集型且通常对环境困难的加工的矿物”。 “然而，许多西方国家花费了数十年的时间，将那些‘肮脏’的工业活动外包出去。” 硫酸在镍和铜等金属加工中也发挥着重要作用，这两种金属广泛用于电动汽车电池和储能系统。 印度尼西亚快速扩张的镍加工业被认为特别容易受到禁令的影响。 中国已成为全球电动汽车（EV）供应链中使用的电池级镍的主要生产国，其中包括与中国电池制造商宁德时代相关的制造商。 将低品位镍矿石精炼成电池材料需要大量硫酸，这一过程被称为高压酸浸出。 如果供应仍然受到限制，炼油厂可能面临更高的生产成本、延误和原料竞争加剧，并可能流向电池制造商和电动汽车……

reflection.en: The halt in sulphuric acid exports highlights the interconnectedness of global supply chains and the importance of foresight. When nations or industries rely heavily on single sources, prudence is needed to anticipate potential disruptions and prepare for their impact.

title.en: As Xi sets a new power dynamic, Trump leaves China with little to brag about
title.zh: 习近平确立新权力格局，特朗普对中国无甚可夸耀

summary.en: A recent summit between the leaders of China and the United States, while largely cordial, indicated a potential shift in the balance of power between the two nations.
summary.zh: 在中美两国领导人的一次大致友好的峰会期间，有迹象表明两国之间的权力平衡可能正在发生变化。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump hailed it as “the biggest summit ever.” In reality, his less than 48 lavish hours in China yielded few results.

Expectations for any real breakthroughs were always low. But what we saw at the high-stakes summit could still shape the US-China relationship for months and years to come.

China had been signalling for weeks that Taiwan would be its top priority at this summit.

The island’s status has always been a point of conflict between the US and Chinese governments; China claims it as a self-governing province that will eventually be brought under its control, while the US has long been its single largest supplier of the weapons needed to prevent that from happening.

But this week, Chinese President Xi Jinping took it one step further; saying explicitly that from now on, the most important factor in the US-China relationship would be how the US deals with Taiwan.

“The Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations,” Xi told Trump, according to the Chinese Foreign Ministry handout. “If it is handled properly, the bilateral relationship will enjoy overall stability. If handled poorly, the two countries will collide or even clash, putting the entire US-China relationship in an extremely dangerous situation.”

When asked for his version of events later in the day, Trump opted to say nothing. His silence was seen as a win in Taiwan, where fears he might go off script and say something to inadvertently shift the US’ position on the island were high going into the summit.

“US policy on the issue of Taiwan is unchanged as of today and as of the meeting that we had here today,” US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said. “It was raised. They always raised it on their side. We always make clear our position and we move on to other topics.”

But China has made its position clear; the US’ ongoing support for Taiwan could jeopardise one of its most important trade relationships.

The US approved a US$15b ($2.09b) arms package for Taiwan in December last year; its largest ever. But with Trump still yet to give his final approval, its delivery had been stalled.

Whether or not those weapons finally reach Taiwan may be the first real test of whether Xi’s threat made an impact.

While the summit was largely cordial, there were moments that signalled the balance of power between the two leaders might be shifting.

Xi rolled out the red carpet and did a lot to make Trump feel respected; sending his Vice President to greet him at the airport, personally accompanying him on a tour of the Temple of Heaven, and allowing him to visit the highly secretive Zhongnanhai compound, where he and other senior Chinese Communist...
body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普称赞这是“有史以来规模最大的峰会”。事实上，他在中国度过的不到48个小时的奢华时光并没有取得什么成果。 对任何真正突破的期望总是很低。但我们在这次高风险峰会上看到的情况仍可能影响未来数月乃至数年的美中关系。 几周来，中国一直在暗示台湾将是此次峰会的首要任务。 该岛的地位一直是美国和中国政府之间的冲突点。中国声称它是一个自治省，最终将受到其控制，而美国长期以来一直是其最大的武器供应商，以防止这种情况发生。 但本周，中国国家主席习近平更进一步；明确表示，今后美中关系最重要的因素将是美国如何对待台湾。 根据中国外交部的讲义，习近平对特朗普说：“台湾问题是中美关系中最重要的问题。” “如果处理得当，双边关系将保持总体稳定。如果处理不好，两国就会发生冲突甚至冲突，使整个美中关系处于极其危险的境地。” 当天晚些时候，当被问及他对事件的看法时，特朗普选择什么也不说。他的沉默在台湾被视为一种胜利，在峰会上，人们非常担心他可能会脱离剧本，说出一些无意中改变美国在台湾的立场的话。 美国国务卿卢比奥表示：“截至今天以及我们今天在这里举行的会议，美国在台湾问题上的政策没有变化。” “有人提出了。他们总是站在自己一边提出。我们总是明确我们的立场，然后转向其他话题。” 但中方已经明确表明立场，美国对台湾的持续支持可能会危及其最重要的贸易关系之一。 去年 12 月，美国批准了一项价值 150 亿美元（2.09b 美元）的台湾军售计划；其规模有史以来最大。但由于特朗普尚未给予最终批准，其交付已陷入停滞。 这些武器最终是否到达台湾可能是习近平的威胁是否产生影响的第一个真正考验。 尽管这次峰会基本上是友好的，但有些时刻表明两位领导人之间的权力平衡可能正在发生变化。 习近平铺上红地毯，做了很多让特朗普感到受到尊重的事情；派副总统到机场迎接他，亲自陪同他游览天坛，并允许他参观高度保密的中南海大院，他和其他中共高级官员都在那里……

reflection.en: News of shifting power dynamics between nations reminds us that human authority is ultimately transient. Psalm 75:7 offers a profound perspective, reminding us that it is God who judges, lifting up one and bringing down another. This truth invites us to look beyond temporary political tides and trust in a higher, unchanging sovereignty.
reflection.zh: 国家间权力动态的变化提醒我们，人类的权威终究是暂时的。诗篇75:7提供了一个深刻的视角，提醒我们是雅伟施行审判，他使这人降卑，使那人升高。这一真理邀请我们超越暂时的政治潮流，信靠那至高无上、永不改变的主权。

verse.textZh: 惟有神断定；他使这人降卑，使那人升高。

title.en: China goes electric, but can it get off coal?

summary.en: The world's clean energy superpower also emits the most CO2. But coal-fired power may have peaked as China electrifies its economy with ever more renewables.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The world's clean energy superpower also emits the most CO2. But coal-fired power may have peaked as China electrifies its economy with ever more renewables.

China is undergoing a renewable energy revolution. In 2025 alone, it added nearly 450 gigawatts (GW) of clean energy capacity, which was more solar and twice as much wind as the rest of the world combined.

Before 2010, China had only limited renewable energy . Today, electricity generated by huge wind and solar farms that stretch out across mountains, deserts, on rooftops and off the coast, account for a quarter of electricity production.

The country achieved the goal of adding 1,200 GW of wind and solar capacity to the grid by 2030 five years ahead of schedule. China also produces over 80% of the world's photovoltaic panels, helping drive down costs and accelerating the clean energy transition globally.

Its quest to rid itself of dependence on foreign oil and gas has been the chief inspiration for the rapid expansion of domestic energy sources and electrification, says Tim Buckley, director of Australian think tank Climate Energy Finance.

Beijing invested early in electric vehicles , and batteries, noted Buckley. Fossil fuel-free vehicles now account for more than half of all car sales in China, compared with about 19% in the European Union.

But the clean energy boom has not displaced coal, the most polluting fossil fuel. The country remains the world's largest emitter of carbon dioxide and continues to exploit its own vast coal reserves in pursuit of energy self-reliance. China consumes over 50% of global supply, in part because it's the only fossil fuel it doesn't have to import. 

In January and February 2026 alone, China added 20 gigawatts of coal-fired power capacity — nearly half the amount of new renewables added over the same period. This partly explains why the country is not on track to meet its 2060 carbon neutrality goal, according to climate think tank, Carbon Tracker. 

The contradiction is at the center of scrutiny over China's latest five year-plan (5YP), a policy blueprint that will shape the economy through 2031 and determine whether the country can meet its climate pledges and help curb planetary heating.  

In 2015, China signed onto the Paris climate agreement, which aims to limit global temperature rise to well below 2 degrees Celsius (3.6 Fahrenheit) or preferably 1.5C, compared to pre-industrial levels. The country then committed to peak CO2 emissions before 2030, and to achieve carbon neutrality by 2060.

title.en: Sydney shooting leaves one person dead, four in hospital
title.zh: 悉尼枪击案造成一人死亡，四人住院

summary.en: Police have established a crime scene at a south-west Sydney home after five men self-presented to hospital on Tuesday night.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
One man has died in hospital and four others are in a serious condition after a shooting in a Sydney home.

Police have set up a crime scene at the home in Canley Heights in south-west Sydney after the men self-presented to two nearby hospitals on Tuesday night. A 28-year-old and a 32-year-old arrived at Liverpool Hospital about 8.30pm AEST with multiple wounds.

While the younger man was treated for a gunshot injury, he died a short time later. The 32-year-old is in hospital with a neck injury and remains in a serious but stable condition.

About 10 minutes after the first two men presented to hospital, two others — a 23-year-old and a 22-year-old — presented to Fairfield Hospital in serious conditions before being moved to other hospitals for further treatment.

The 23-year-old received care for a gunshot wound to the neck, and the other was treated for a shoulder injury.

The fifth man, a 19-year-old, arrived at Liverpool Hospital an hour later with injuries to his arm, and remains in a stable condition.

"Initial information indicates the men were all injured during a shooting at the home earlier in the night," NSW Police said in a statement.

Officers were seen swarming around the hospitals' emergency wards in the late hours of the night as an investigation into the incident was launched.

NSW Police commissioner Mal Lanyon told 2GB radio on Wednesday that the motive was unclear, but it appeared to be a "targeted attack" and suggested it could be related to organised crime.

title.en: 'Our business partner, Anthony Albanese': The 47 per cent tax claim going viral after the budget

summary.en: Startup founders and small business owners have spread AI-generated memes about proposed changes to the capital gains tax.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
AI-generated memes mocking the federal government's proposed capital gains tax reforms are spreading on social media as businesses fear how the changes could affect them.

Startup founders and small business owners who have taken part in the trend say Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is becoming a "47 per cent silent partner" in their businesses due to the proposed restructure — something experts say is an overstatement.

The viral campaign includes edited images of Albanese performing everyday business tasks such as serving customers, laying concrete, cooking pizzas, and stocking shelves. The captions suggest the government would take almost half of any profits from future business sales.

Carlos Cordova has run a food business for almost a decade, and told SBS News: "All of our savings and holiday savings and little getaway savings have gone into the business."

"We’re finding it harder to keep up, really. We’re finding it tough to stay ahead of the game."

Cordova said he voted for Labor, thinking that the CGT changes wouldn't be made. He said he was "lied to" and "won't be voting Labor any time soon".

Cordova took part in the AI meme trend, posting a fake image of himself with the prime minister on social media over the weekend.

"We would like to formally welcome our new business partner, Anthony Albanese," it reads.

"After Janet and I spent just under 8 years building Sur Direct from the ground up, the markets, the manufacturing, the sleepless nights, the risks, the sacrifices, we thought it only made sense to partner up and basically hand over 47% of the business."

This social media trend grew after last week's federal budget , when changes to CGT were announced. Labor had ruled out changes in the lead-up to last year's federal election.

The government has proposed replacing Australia's long-standing 50 per cent capital gains tax discount with a new inflation-linked system. Under the proposed changes, some high-income earners could face tax rates of up to 47 per cent on certain capital gains.

However, experts say the memes exaggerate the impact of the changes as the reforms apply to profits from the sale of assets, not to regular business income or daily profits. They also say many small businesses would still qualify for existing tax concessions.

Independent economist Saul Eslake said the suggestion that reforms would somehow make the government or the prime minister a 47 per cent shareholder in every business is "completely fictitious".

"What you pay capital gains tax on is the increase in the value of assets which you own when you sell them," he explained to SBS News.

"Under the changes the government is proposing, Australians will get relief from the impact of inflation on the cost base of those assets.

title.en: A dangerous communist label — and the Australian funding facing scrutiny
